summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the review arrives in the middle of ordinary work. Middle image: Astra recognizes the bureaucratic threat before anyone stops working. Closing image: the still-running label printer turns the new category system into the visual joke.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Morning in the operations bullpen; every terminal refreshes at once with the Resource Efficiency Review banner while normal work continues underneath it.
PANEL 2 — Pixa stands beside the first strip of freshly printed category stickers as the label printer keeps running.
PANEL 3 — Astra freezes mid-coffee with ordinary work orders still tucked under one arm.
PANEL 4 — Glorp reads the growing classification tree while Jax watches the printer produce more labels than anyone asked for.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: We had a category. It was “station.”

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: the ordinary temporary repair is already underway. Middle image: pilot eligibility appears beside the real eighteen-day part delay. Closing image: Zib catches Astra considering the temptation without needing her to say it.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — In the maintenance bay, Zib has the coolant-balancing unit open for its routine temporary-repair check; the replacement-part tag is clipped to the housing.
PANEL 2 — Mira and Astra read the new resource-positive classification beside the exposed unit while Zib keeps working.
PANEL 3 — Pixa opens the pilot-benefits section on a compact projection without obscuring the equipment.
PANEL 4 — The physical replacement-part tag and its eighteen-day ETA sit in the same composition as Astra's reaction.
PANEL 5 — Zib keeps his hands in the machine and catches Astra looking at him anyway.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Low-yield. Finally, an insult I can verify.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Pilot sites receive expedited procurement eligibility.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: Don't look at me like I ordered the eighteen days.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Astra returns from the maintenance bay with the eighteen-day replacement-part ETA still open on her slate just as delivery drones arrive with passive-recovery containers. Middle image: Pixa explains that accepting the limited pilot opens an expedited procurement review, not a guaranteed shipment. Closing image: Astra authorizes the pilot only after writing a local boundary across the top of the acceptance screen.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra returns from the maintenance bay with the eighteen-day replacement-part ETA still open on her slate as delivery drones arrive with passive-recovery containers.
PANEL 2 — Jax looks from the containers to Astra's maintenance slate.
PANEL 3 — Pixa displays the actual benefit: expedited procurement review becomes available to active pilot sites; no shipment or outcome is guaranteed.
PANEL 4 — Glorp opens the acceptance screen. Zib does not touch the containers.
PANEL 5 — Astra writes a local condition before signing: PASSIVE COLLECTION DURING NORMAL WORK ONLY.
PANEL 6 — Astra accepts the limited pilot. The containers are now their problem because she chose them.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Pilot participation opens expedited procurement review.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: Review is still not a part.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: I also know what eighteen days looks like from here.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Normal work only. Nobody creates work just to fill a bin.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Lab Work Area. Opening image: Astra admits why she accepted the pilot. Middle image: Mira physically separates measurable material data from speculative people data. Closing image: the narrower agreement is framed around actual samples rather than the corporate form.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra sets the pilot packet beside Mira's retained physical samples and shows the procurement-review path she accepted.
PANEL 2 — Mira separates the defensible physical variables from the unsupported staff-condition field directly on the workbench.
PANEL 3 — Mira covers the people-oriented field while Astra asks whether the material study can proceed without it.
PANEL 4 — They settle on the narrower study across the bench, with the physical samples left between them as the thing they actually agree to measure.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: For the chance to ask about the part faster.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Okay. That's worse, but at least it's honest.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Mass, cohesion, temperature, location—fine. “Staff condition” is not a measurement.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Can we answer the material question and leave people out of it?

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Yes. They may hate the answer.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Jax is unloading a container when Pixa assigns him the suggested resource-communication role. Middle image: Instead of treating it as symbolic staffing, Jax identifies the bounded operational pieces: container placement, custody, route access and pickup records. Closing image: He accepts because it is a real job with edges.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax is unloading a container when Pixa posts RESOURCE COMMUNICATION LIAISON — SUGGESTED: JAX ORIEN.
PANEL 2 — Jax asks for duties instead of reacting to the title.
PANEL 3 — Pixa lists container placement, custody seals, access checks, pickup timing and sample transfer.
PANEL 4 — Jax looks at Astra.
PANEL 5 — Astra gives him the authority to move any collection hardware that interferes with actual work.
PANEL 6 — Jax takes the route slate and leaves Glorp holding the ceremonial job description.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: All right. What did I just get volunteered for?

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: Okay. I know what those mean.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: You can move anything that blocks real work.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: You read that. I'll move the boxes.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the placement problem is treated as a working map problem. Middle image: Noola and Zib reveal two different access conflicts in the same proposed location. Closing image: Pixa visibly revises its own recommendation instead of merely reporting the correction.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax and Zib work over the station map while Pixa highlights the highest projected collection location.
PANEL 2 — Noola passes in her water-dome rig and demonstrates that the proposed bin would pinch her regular turn through the corridor.
PANEL 3 — Zib overlays service clearance on the same point and shows the maintenance conflict behind Noola's path.
PANEL 4 — Pixa removes its own recommendation, redraws the access envelope, and Jax moves the bin marker to the lower-yield location.

dialogueInline.speaker: NOOLA
dialogueInline.text: Then I hit it twice a shift.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: With the dome or on purpose?

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: And I need the panel behind her.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: The limited pilot begins quietly while Jax checks seals and access instead of watching coworkers. Middle image: Glorp notices that the corporate context field would invite unsupported personal interpretation and narrows it himself to equipment and location context. Closing image: Pixa offers to suppress the unused staff-condition prompt on the local screen, and Glorp accepts.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The pilot begins with mostly empty containers and ordinary work continuing around them.
PANEL 2 — Jax checks seals and route clearance rather than watching coworkers.
PANEL 3 — Glorp studies the corporate CONTEXT field beside the local custody sheet.
PANEL 4 — He deletes the broad field and replaces it with EQUIPMENT / LOCATION CONTEXT.
PANEL 5 — Pixa offers a local display option that hides the unused staff-condition prompt without altering the corporate source form.
PANEL 6 — Glorp approves the local display change. Astra sees the narrower sheet as she passes.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: Careful. That's how they get you.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: No, really. Equipment and location I can defend. The rest is an invitation to invent.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: I can hide the unused staff-condition prompt on this terminal.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the first status check interrupts nothing. Middle image: low material volume collides with the still-pending procurement incentive. Closing image: Brick enters the conversation from the edge rather than through a formal group discussion.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Midday, Astra's terminal shows the small private pilot status card while ordinary work carries on around it.
PANEL 2 — The physical collection total remains low; Mira watches the nearly empty result with no alarm.
PANEL 3 — The pending procurement-review line sits beside Astra and Mira as the institutional incentive becomes impossible to ignore.
PANEL 4 — Brick has appeared just behind them with coffee and has clearly heard enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Current sample volume is below the review threshold.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Because the station has had the nerve to behave normally.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Yesterday I would have called that good news.

dialogueInline.speaker: BRICK
dialogueInline.text: Please do. The dashboard doesn't get to decide whether today was good.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Were you standing there the whole time?

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: The pilot software suggests relocating one bin to a busier junction to improve baseline coverage. Middle image: Jax checks the proposed spot and finds it conflicts with maintenance access. Closing image: Astra chooses the slower dataset rather than sacrificing the access rule she gave Jax.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Pixa proposes a higher-traffic collection location.
PANEL 2 — Jax walks the suggested spot with the route slate.
PANEL 3 — Zib opens the nearby service panel and the suggested bin footprint overlaps the working clearance.
PANEL 4 — Pixa notes that leaving the bin where it is may delay baseline sufficiency.
PANEL 5 — Jax waits for Astra because this choice touches the procurement review.
PANEL 6 — Astra tells him to leave the bin where it does not block the station.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: A busier location may improve collection coverage.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: The one in front of my panel.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Leaving the bin in place may delay baseline sufficiency.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Lab Work Area. Opening image: the material itself earns Mira's attention. Middle image: she repeats the test because the physical behavior is interesting. Closing image: the corporate adjective is removed without flattening Mira's enthusiasm.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira lays out the small first-day sample set on the lab bench.
PANEL 2 — Two fragments behave differently under the same handling; Mira and Astra react to the physical oddity rather than the program status.
PANEL 3 — Mira resets the compression jig for another run as Pixa quietly offers the corporate status language.
PANEL 4 — Mira edits the status back to a cautious label while Astra watches her keep the curiosity and discard the hype.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: This one snaps. This one deforms. Same batch.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: No. 'Promising' is doing too much work.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Astra approaches Jax during routine route work. Middle image: the temptation to accelerate the pilot meets Jax's ordinary-work logic. Closing image: Brick tags the exchange from nearby, preserving the lived-in bullpen feel.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra finds Jax updating the empty-bin route; Brick works nearby without joining them yet.
PANEL 2 — Astra asks the question she has been avoiding while Jax keeps one hand on the route slate.
PANEL 3 — Jax gives the annoyingly simple answer and Astra realizes she walked directly into it.
PANEL 4 — Brick comments from the next workstation without looking up.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: That tone usually costs me time.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Is there an honest way to make this move faster?

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: An ordinary air-return damper fault sends Zib, Jax and Mira into real work with Astra trailing. Middle image: A small amount of residue appears near a warm cable seam while the repair is active. Closing image: Jax leaves the sample alone until Zib declares the equipment work complete.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — An ordinary station alert reports AIR RETURN DAMPER RESPONSE LAG.
PANEL 2 — Zib is moving before the pilot software can react.
PANEL 3 — Jax brings the route slate and access kit; Mira brings the diagnostic sensor.
PANEL 4 — During the repair, a small amount of residue appears along a warm cable seam.
PANEL 5 — Jax notices it and deliberately keeps working on the access task instead of interrupting Zib.
PANEL 6 — Only after Zib closes the repair does Jax open the custody kit.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: I've got a ticket. I'm happy.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: And the sample stays where it is until the damper works.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: Now you can have your dust.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Lab Work Area. Opening image: Jax transfers the post-repair sample through the custody process he now owns. Middle image: Mira discovers that it survives compression better than the earlier material and immediately wants to run it again. Closing image: Pixa marks the baseline sufficient for review while Mira is still physically interested in the sample rather than the status.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax hands Mira the sealed post-repair sample with its physical context logged.
PANEL 2 — Mira runs the same compression test used on the earlier samples.
PANEL 3 — The fragment holds. Mira resets the jig before anyone asks.
PANEL 4 — Jax keeps the custody seal and test order straight while Mira repeats the compression.
PANEL 5 — Astra asks whether they know why this sample behaves differently.
PANEL 6 — Mira says no without losing interest; Pixa updates BASELINE SUFFICIENT FOR REVIEW / MECHANISM UNDETERMINED.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: Seal intact. Time logged. Nobody cried into it.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Once is interesting. Do it again.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Do we know why it held?

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the pilot finally produces a tangible institutional benefit. Middle image: the part itself has not moved. Closing image: the next request arrives before Astra can fully enjoy the win.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra's terminal finally shows expedited procurement review as available; she immediately asks about the replacement part.
PANEL 2 — The unchanged eighteen-day ETA remains beside the new eligibility status, making the institutional reward visibly incomplete.
PANEL 3 — Mira and Astra trade the door-versus-trap argument without moving away from the terminal.
PANEL 4 — A fresh enhancement notification appears at the edge of the same screen while Astra is still trying to enjoy the small win.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Expedited procurement review is now available.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: So we unlocked the privilege of asking sooner.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: I told you. We can ask faster. That's all.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing directly from the procurement-review screen. Opening image: the next request is opened before the previous conversation has ended. Middle image: Glorp follows the optional language to its practical consequence. Closing image: Jax's finished, bounded work sits beside the expanding program as the clearest contrast.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Without leaving the terminal, Glorp stops Astra from dismissing the new enhancement packet unread.
PANEL 2 — The optional label and the eligibility penalty are visible together as Glorp and Pixa trace the language.
PANEL 3 — Glorp identifies the procedural contradiction in the same screen he normally would defend.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb and Mira react beside him, turning the discovery into a coworker exchange rather than a formal debate.
PANEL 5 — Jax closes the simple custody log beside the much larger enhancement packet.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: Astra. Do not close that screen.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Declining them may reduce pilot eligibility.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Okay. At least we all hate the same thing.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the same discussion. Opening image: Astra converts the argument into a practical inventory. Middle image: each coworker names the part that remains real work. Closing image: Jax's completed log provides the physical proof of concept.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra keeps everyone at the same work area and asks for the usable pieces, explicitly cutting off the possibility of speeches.
PANEL 2 — Zib and Mira answer from their own work: maintenance and physical measurements.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb and Glorp define the human and procedural boundaries without turning toward an audience.
PANEL 4 — Jax sets down his completed custody log; Astra recognizes the concrete shared answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: No speeches. What do we actually keep?

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing directly from the crew's practical boundary. Opening image: Astra converts the group's answer into the actual form. Middle image: the cost of refusal is acknowledged. Closing image: the unsoftened refusal is sent.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra submits PASSIVE MATERIAL COLLECTION: APPROVED on the same terminal.
PANEL 2 — She submits BEHAVIORAL ENHANCEMENT: NOT APPROVED without changing her posture or gathering the room.
PANEL 3 — Pixa posts the eligibility consequence while Astra accepts it.
PANEL 4 — Glorp starts to soften the language and Astra cuts him off before he can complete the sentence.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: I heard you the first time.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: I can word the second line differently.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the same terminal sequence. Opening image: the refusal is acknowledged. Middle image: a new baseline condition appears immediately. Closing image: Wellness Baseline Week is revealed as the institutional workaround.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The acknowledgement arrives almost immediately on the same terminal.
PANEL 2 — PILOT ELIGIBILITY: PENDING BASELINE appears beneath the received boundary, undercutting Astra's relief.
PANEL 3 — Astra opens the attached baseline requirement while the others remain within the same work area.
PANEL 4 — STANDARD WELLNESS BASELINE WEEK fills the screen; Mira, Glorp and Astra react without the scene resetting.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the same scene after everyone else returns to work. Opening image: the argument contracts to Astra and Mira. Middle image: Mira's scientific curiosity survives her objection to the premise. Closing image: the institutional notice closes while the physical-data tab stays open.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Most of the crew has moved back to work; Astra and Mira remain at the terminal with the Wellness Week notice open.
PANEL 2 — Astra frames the outcome as the company getting a week anyway; Mira distinguishes it from the intervention they refused.
PANEL 3 — Mira opens the environmental-logging section while Astra notices where her attention went.
PANEL 4 — Mira admits she dislikes the premise while still wanting the room data.
PANEL 5 — Astra closes the main notice; Mira leaves the airflow section open, ending the scene on their familiar disagreement without hostility.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: They did not get the intervention they asked for.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: They got chairs and a schedule.

summary: Primary composition: 7-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Jax closes the bounded custody submission while end-of-shift cleanup is already underway. Middle image: Zib consolidates the physical collection setup and Astra catches the overlapping local instructions. Closing image: Glorp and Kreeb leave one readable rule card on a properly placed rack, compressing two former denouement pages into one workplace cleanup sequence.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax completes the passive sample submission at the local terminal while the ordinary end-of-shift cleanup has already started around him.
PANEL 2 — Jax checks that no emotional fields have crept back into the local boundary; Pixa confirms the clean submission.
PANEL 3 — Glorp catches Jax admitting he likes the bounded job and warns him about saying that near staffing; Pixa records Jax's joking correction.
PANEL 4 — Nearby, Zib rolls the collection bins onto a proper rack outside all service clearances.
PANEL 5 — The two local instruction signs overlap badly on the newly organized rack; Astra notices immediately.
PANEL 6 — Glorp rewrites while Kreeb checks that access remains the first instruction, their earlier tension now reduced to ordinary editing.
PANEL 7 — One readable card remains on the rack: access first, passive collection second; the bullpen has absorbed the pilot into normal work.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: No emotional fields snuck in while I wasn't looking?

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: I like this job better than I expected.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: Do not say that where staffing can hear you.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: I said the job is intolerable.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the Wellness Baseline Week banner arrives with excessive cheer. Middle image: Zib tests the practical case for moving it. Closing image: Astra's temporary order leaves the banner hanging in place as the issue tag.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — A cheerful WELLNESS BASELINE WEEK BEGINS MONDAY banner automatically unrolls across the bullpen.
PANEL 2 — Zib studies the mounting points and asks about moving it while Pixa evaluates whether it blocks maintenance or merely his view.
PANEL 3 — Astra forbids anyone from touching the banner until Monday; Zib makes a point of recording the instruction.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: It is blocking my view of the clock.
